To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction of Cu2+ ions with calf thymus-DNA leads to the formation of sandwich-type complexes, where the metal ion is inserted into a GpG step.

the interaction of DNA with Cu2+, which is a model system for the interaction of DNA and other biomolecules with metal ions, results in the formation of chelates in which the Cu2+ ions are coordinated to phosphate groups at low ion concentrations.
the interaction of DNA with copper(II) ions leads to a significant distortion of the DNA structure at high metal concentrations, which is most pronounced for guanine-cytidine base pairs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between DNA and Cu2+ ions in aqueous solutions at room temperature.
the interaction of Cu2+ ions with calf thymus (CT) DNA at room temperature in aqueous solution.
the study of the interaction between DNA and metal ions and the influence of the metal ions on the structure of DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA structure is significantly affected at a [Cu2+]/[phosphate] ratio of 1/2 and above.
the DNA structure is not a single well-defined conformation but is a dynamic ensemble of different conformations, depending on the Cu2+ concentration.

the DNA secondary structure changes from the standard B form to a partially denatured structure with a significant fraction of stacked and paired GC base pairs, possibly in a "sandwich-like" conformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VCD and simultaneous IR spectroscopy can be applied to study the structural changes of DNA upon binding of metal ions, and the VCD spectra provide additional information about the 3-dimensional DNA structure.
the Cu2+ ion binds to phosphate groups and to guanines at low metal concentrations and that the DNA structure becomes significantly altered at a [Cu]2+ / [P] ratio of approximately 0.5.
the VCD spectra are very sensitive to the DNA secondary structure, whereas IR absorption spectra are more sensitive to the DNA tertiary structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VCD spectra of DNA complexes with metal ions can be used as a sensitive tool to study DNA-metal interactions.
the DNA structure is very sensitive to Cu2+ binding and that the VCD technique can be applied to study the structure of DNA complexes with other metal ions.
VCD is a very useful tool for the study of metal ion-DNA interactions.
